claims.statement: The modular documentation contract `.agent-harness/documentation/manifest.json` (schema_version 1) defines six families — ADR, ARCHITECTURE, CAUTIONS, CONVENTIONS, OPERATIONS, TESTING — each pairing a required root index with its module directory, with `max_root_lines` and `max_module_lines` budgets of 250 and a `single_owner_topics` map for COMMIT_POLICY, CONSTITUTION, OPEN_API_SPEC, TECH_STACK, and AGENT_WORKFLOW.

Each family root index owns only the short normative summary, links into its module directory, and family update instructions; detailed modules own procedures, rationale, examples, and dated records and link back to their root, with cross-family references carrying only a link to the canonical owner. The 250-line budget is a retrieval boundary: an oversized module must be split by responsibility, not truncated.

The agent-harness repository itself dogfoods the manifest contract: its `.agent-harness/` tree contains all six family roots plus their module directories, and `.agent-harness/documentation/` carries manifest.json, the responsibility audit (AUDIT.md, which measured the pre-modularization monoliths such as a 956-line ADR.md), and README.md owning the navigation model. The repo-owned manifest extends the five seeded single-owner topics with two audit-record entries (`archive/issueops-audit.md` and root-retained `PROJECT_AUDIT.md`, parsed in place by `quality inspect`).

Default native install writes nothing into a target repository: host installers plan only user-level skill symlinks, MCP registration, lifecycle hooks, and in-repo templates under `configs/`; repo-local files (`.mcp.json`, `.claude/skills/`, `.omo/`) are created only on explicit `--project-local`. The install contract matrix asserts default install leaves those repo paths absent, and the installer prints that project-local repo files are unchanged by default.

The only paths that create repo files besides the project-local install opt-in are `agent-harness project bootstrap` (and its MCP plan form `project_docs_bootstrap_plan`), where `--dry-run` previews the plan without writing and `--sync` is an explicit opt-in to refresh existing generated docs.

Bootstrap manages AGENTS.md through its `AGENT_HARNESS:START`/`AGENT_HARNESS:END` marker block only, never the whole file: the routing block (doc-per-concern bullets) is replaced between markers, existing content is preserved, the generic behavioral template is prepended only when the file does not already open with its own `# ` heading, and a missing AGENTS.md is created from the behavioral guidelines plus the routing block.

Folder-first family roots and module starters are create-only artifacts: bootstrap writes them only when absent and never updates them, even under `--sync`; an attempted family update reports `family_docs_preserved` and routes curation to `project_docs_revise` or `project-docs-optimize`, while non-family generated docs are preserved with a `sync_available` warning unless `--sync` is passed.

Bootstrap preserves a legacy flat layout — family roots present without `documentation/manifest.json` — instead of half-migrating it: it emits `legacy_flat_layout_preserved` and skips module-starter and manifest seeding; restructuring belongs to project-docs-optimize, not bootstrap.

The manifest is seeded once by bootstrap and then repo-owned: `--sync` over an existing manifest reports `manifest_preserved` rather than resetting budgets that the repo or project-docs-optimize may have tuned by hand.

Bootstrap plans from repository evidence: AnalyzeProjectSignals walks known signal files up to depth 4 (go.mod, package.json, pyproject.toml, Cargo.toml, CI workflows, task runners, existing agent docs), deriving languages, package managers, and test/build/lint command candidates each tagged with evidence and confidence, plus a profile (VCS provider from the git origin, project types, frameworks, monorepo) that also seeds the repo-scoped lifecycle namespace and persisted repo metadata in user-state.

Every standard project doc carries canonical, name-keyed meta frontmatter (`name:` plus a fixed one-line `description:` per doc name, identical across repos and stable across bootstrap and --sync). EnsureMetaFrontmatter runs on the write pass for even preserved docs, and the hook catalog falls back to the same name-keyed table when a doc's frontmatter lacks a description.

Only VCS.md and DESIGN.md are optional project docs: DESIGN.md (design-system contract) is rendered only when the profile detects a client surface (frontend or desktop-client), and bootstrap never creates VCS.md — route-docs attaches it only for VCS-related tasks.

`agent-harness docs [index] [--json]` indexes the harness corpus (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, GENIUS_THINK.md, `.agent-harness/` markdown, skills/self-verify, skills/self-augment) with rel path, first level-1 title, up to 20 headings, and size, sorted by path. The index is hermetic: candidates are filtered to git-tracked files using root-relative, NUL-delimited `git ls-files` matching, falling back to all candidates when git is unavailable or the tracked set matches nothing; `.agent-harness/draft-wiki` and `.agent-harness/evidence` are always excluded so untracked session artifacts cannot drift the index.

The docs index is a golden-pinned response contract: CLI `docs --json` and MCP `docs_index` responses are snapshotted into `cmd/harness/testdata/response_contracts.golden.json` via a projection that pins required entrypoints (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, the .agent-harness roots, self-verify/self-augment skill docs) while numeric docs_count/docs_indexed values are replaced with a `$DOCS_COUNT` placeholder (the structural fix for #109's per-commit golden churn); a non-numeric counter still fails the gate as a contract regression.

The MCP surface re-exposes the same doc readers: the `docs_index` tool and `harness://docs` resource both call docs.DocsIndex over the harness root, `harness://project-docs` returns the default (general) route, and `harness://project-doc-upkeep` carries the route → read → revise/append upkeep guidance; maintenance tools are `project_docs_route`, `project_docs_read`, `project_docs_revise`, `project_docs_append`, and `project_docs_bootstrap_plan`.

`agent-harness project route-docs --repo PATH --task TEXT` maps a task to owning documents instead of injecting every doc: AGENTS.md is always routed, keyword rules select sets (e.g. commit|pr|push → COMMIT_POLICY+TESTING+CAUTIONS; test|spec|verify|ci → TESTING+TECH_STACK+AGENT_WORKFLOW+CAUTIONS; VCS keywords add optional VCS.md), unknown tasks fall back to the CONSTITUTION/AGENT_WORKFLOW/CONVENTIONS/CAUTIONS/TESTING set, and when a routed family root's overview module exists it is attached automatically so agents read actual detail. Entries report existence, and a missing `.agent-harness/` directory produces a warning pointing at bootstrap.

Default installs register exactly one lifecycle hook event per host — SessionStart in ~/.codex/hooks.json and ~/.claude/settings.json — invoking `agent-harness hook session-start --host codex|claude` with a 5-second timeout, because both hosts re-run SessionStart with source "compact" after compaction and only SessionStart output carries model-facing additionalContext there; `hook post-compact` remains for hosts without a re-run (Omo) and diagnosis, and HARNESS_DISABLE_HOOKS=1 turns both hooks into no-ops.

The hook injects a menu, not a relevance decision: DiscoverProjectDocs scans only the working repo's top-level `.agent-harness/*.md` (rejecting symlinks, bounded at 64 entries, 256 KiB per file, 2 MiB total, deterministically sorted) and describes each doc by frontmatter description or the canonical name-keyed table; BuildProjectDocCatalogContext produces a compact model-facing menu and readable user view and sets ShouldInject=false when no docs exist, leaving the choice of what to read to the agent.

`project_docs_append` normalizes record kinds to caution or adr and always writes one dated, collision-suffixed record file (`adr/YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>.md`, `cautions/YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>.md`) with canonical record frontmatter into the family module directory, never touching the family root index — so append cannot churn the root SHA other agents hold — and there is no flat-layout fallback even in repos without a manifest or bootstrap.

`project_docs_revise` gates full-document replacement on consensus: updating an existing doc requires `expected_sha256` from a prior `project_docs_read` (a mismatch refuses the write), a non-empty summary, and `confirm=true`; without confirm it is a dry-run reporting the prospective `next_sha256` without writing.

Rel-path normalization accepts the required and optional doc names plus any family module document path (e.g. adr/2026-08-20-slug.md, testing/overview.md) — rejecting traversal and non-markdown targets — so the read/revise contract can address record files and module starters in folder-first repositories; `project append` is the CLI fallback for records, and full-document revision has no CLI surface.

Four skills map onto the CLI/MCP surfaces in a create → refresh → restructure lifecycle: `project-bootstrap` orchestrates and owns lifecycle routing (missing docs or explicit refresh → project-docs-bootstrap; completed work produced a caution/ADR/stale section → project-docs-update; over-budget roots, duplicated ownership, or checker violations → project-docs-optimize); each sub-skill is usable standalone and wraps one deterministic surface.

project-docs-bootstrap runs the deterministic CLI pass then an agent enrichment pass (PROMPT.md) with a fixed boundary: the static pass fills only skeletons, detected signals, candidate commands, routing, generic guidance, and managed AGENTS.md blocks, while the agent fills actual architecture, operations, conventions, testing, and cautions/ADRs from repository evidence; the engineering-standards catalog is a checklist — each topic must be evidence-confirmed and written to its single owning document, unconfirmed topics are marked `Unknown / not confirmed`, and repo conventions and doc language always outrank harness defaults.

The project-docs-optimize checker (`skills/project-docs-optimize/scripts/check.py`, --mode report|check) executes the manifest contract against `.agent-harness/**.md` plus root AGENTS.md: it reports missing_root, line_budget_exceeded for roots and modules, missing_module_dir, empty_module_dir, module_dir_unlinked (root must link into its module dir), missing_owner for single-owner topics, and broken_link for every local markdown target; check mode exits non-zero on any violation.

`agent-harness doctor` checks project-doc and lifecycle state: missing standard docs are reported as the `project_docs_missing` warning whose fix is `agent-harness project bootstrap`, an uninitialized project lifecycle namespace or a fingerprint mismatch surface as `lifecycle_state_missing`/`lifecycle_namespace_mismatch` pointing at bootstrap, and repo-local runtime artifacts (`.agent-harness/state`, `state.schema.json`, schema-talk in STATE.md) are flagged as `repo_local_state_present` to keep docs and runtime state separated.

Editing `.agent-harness/*.md` can drift response-contract goldens because the docs index feeds them: removing or renaming a tracked required doc changes the pinned required_docs projection, and a regression making a docs counter non-numeric fails the placeholder gate; the documented update workflow runs `agent-harness docs --json`, command smoke checks, and the optimize checker after doc changes.

Doc readers are injected at the composition root rather than imported by consumers: configureDocsReaders installs docs.DocsIndex into mcpcli, basiccli, the self-augment planner/catalog, qagate, and inspect; configureProjectDocReaders installs DiscoverProjectDocs/FormatProjectDocCatalog into the hook prompt layer and PlannedFileAction into both bootstrap and projectdocs; the CLI facade passes DocsIndex into basiccli.Configure.

project-docs-update keeps docs current during work without restructuring: it routes first, reads with SHA, then appends cautions/ADRs by default or revises one document at a time; it never edits AGENTS.md outside the behavioral top block and managed marker block, never moves or splits files (that belongs to project-docs-optimize), and refuses CAUTIONS/ADR updates for hypothetical rather than concrete solved cases.
